title: The Source Where Language Still Stammers

features.name: first stammer
features.desc-on-touch: The sound before it became a word. Here the river begins to speak, but syllables haven't crystallized yet. You hear meaning forming in real time, liquid and unfinished.

features.name: proto-grammar emerging
features.desc-on-touch: The archive here is not yet speech. It is the moment when sound discovers it could be language. Grammar is forming from the river's own repetition, variation, and return.

features.name: roar becoming grammar
features.desc-on-touch: The place where the river's physical sound begins teaching itself language. Each repetition is a lesson; each variation is a new grammar trying to hold the flood.

features.name: meaning congealing
features.desc-on-touch: Droplets of sense gathering into words. This is the archive's root moment—the instant when sound discovers it can mean. Before this, there was only the river. After, there is language.

features.name: liquid lexicon root
features.desc-on-touch: The first word-shapes forming from flowing water. Each one slips back into the current before it can fully crystallize. The river is still teaching language to speak itself.

inscription: the roar has not yet decided which word it will become

file.name: River_Source_Audio_Proto-Phoneme_Spectrogram.mp3
file.note: The archive's first recording. Before grammar. Sound discovering it could be language. The spectrogram shows patterns forming and dissolving each moment.
